command.mac:
Probe for step c107 (an orchestrator starts its lanes with no click). Run on this Mac, in the desktop app Code tab, in Bypass permissions mode. My typing this message is my ask in words for the test sessions below.

Facts so far: the docs name no setting for `mcp__ccd_session__start_session`. Candidate causes: (a) the tool is flagged `_meta["anthropic/requiresUserInteraction"]` (docs: prompts on every call, even in Bypass, and allow rules and PreToolUse "allow" do not skip it); (b) the open "desktop actions" clause of Bypass; (c) the `kind` value.

Do these in order. Stop at the first step where no card shows. Before each start, say "probe N" and after it say "card: yes/no" from what I tell you or what the call returned. Ask me one line only: "Did a card show for probe N? y/n".

0. Record: `claude --version` and the app version. Find the tool's entry (ToolSearch "select:mcp__ccd_session__start_session", or list the app MCP tools) and say whether its description or metadata shows `requiresUserInteraction`.
1. Probe 1, as is: start one session, kind `user_asked`, prompt "Reply ok and stop." Ask me about the card.
2. Probe 2, allow rule: add `"mcp__ccd_session__start_session"` to `permissions.allow` in `~/.claude/settings.local.json` (back up the file first). Start another session the same way. Ask me.
3. Probe 3, hook: add a PreToolUse hook in `~/.claude/settings.local.json` with matcher `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` that prints `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow"}}`. Start another. Ask me.
4. Probe 4, a start call carrying `source_branch` and `branch_name`: check the new session is on that branch (the card has dropped it before).
5. Restore `~/.claude/settings.local.json` from the backup. Never edit `~/.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` or the claude-settings repo.

Report (12 lines max): per probe, card yes/no and branch kept yes/no; the verdict, one of "setting X removes the card" (give the exact lines) or "product limit: the tool always asks" (cite step 0). If a setting works, the fix goes in the repo's settings.json through a draft PR by a lane, not by you. Send the report to the Coordinator session_013NEJL1gw6EdrSyvHkTUEx6.
If it is a product limit, the workaround stays as ruled: an orchestrator starts lanes as background Agent spawns with `isolation: 'worktree'` and uses start_session only on my words.
